chapter: Building the band in New York
title: Who created the themes: Lester Young's melodic solos
summary: Basie says many players had ideas, and Prez's solo lines were so melodic that they could be hummed.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: And where would the lines come from? The themes?
Well, things came out. I mean, maybe somebody else had a theme line.
Uh-huh. Who was the most inventive with theme lines in the band, in the early band?
I don't know. I think there's a lot of guys that had ideas in there, you know. Most everybody had little ideas of something. No matter how small it was, you know.
In the early days, how many themes
Oh, I don't know. Prez had (Inaudible) a lot of themes (inaudible). A lot of things should have been themes.
I don't know, it's (inaudible). It was just something you played and then you could hear it on the record.
And this comes down in his solos. Not that he'd sit down and would say, 'Here, man, let's do,' you know.

But there's some things, some lines that he would play in his solos. And it became a thing that people could whistle and hum his solos. That's the way he played. I mean, (inaudible) all down through the years. I mean, anybody play a record of Prez, everybody could (inaudible) whistle or hum his solo because it's such a melodic (inaudible) line.
